findings.evidence: "... the bottleneck-regime difference is the primary motivation for disaggregation — see §6 for the conditions under which it pays."
findings.issue: Bare section pointer "§6" inside Chapter 6 is self-referential and malformed per the book's own convention ("§N.M refers to chapter N, section M"). A reader cannot resolve it, and the intended destination (likely §6.6 Architecture Consequence) is not identified.
findings.fix_instruction: Replace "see §6" with the specific target section, e.g. "see §6.6".

findings.evidence: "This is precisely why Splitwise/DistServe (and Mooncake's KV-centric disaggregation) split prefill from decode onto different pools: the bottleneck-regime difference is the primary motivation for disaggregation — see §6 for the conditions under which it pays. [S4][1P][FACT]"
findings.issue: Label [1P][FACT] is attached to a paragraph that includes the author's causal interpretation ("This is precisely why ...") and a forward pointer. The interpretive sentence is not a first-party fact.
findings.fix_instruction: Attach [1P][FACT] only to the factual source claim about the systems, and leave the interpretive sentence unlabeled or mark it [DERIVED].

findings.evidence: p.110 (Ch 6 §6.3.3): "Splitwise/DistServe (and Mooncake's KV-centric disaggregation) split prefill from decode onto different pools: the bottleneck-regime difference is the primary motivation for disaggregation — see §6 for the conditions under which it pays."
findings.issue: Bare '§6' cross-reference that does not follow the stated § N.M convention (p.14: 'a bare § N.M refers to chapter N, section M'). The reference lacks a section number. It most likely means §6.6 (Architecture Consequence) which discusses the conditions for P/D disaggregation, but as written it is malformed and ambiguous (chapter 6 with missing section? or section 6 of the current chapter?).
findings.fix_instruction: Change 'see §6' to 'see §6.6' (the Architecture Consequence section that discusses the conditions for P/D disaggregation) to conform to the § N.M convention stated on p.14.

findings.evidence: On the canonical 8×H100 host the aggregate peak is ~7.9 PFLOPS, so the host comfortably satisfies the rate — the 'single H100 can't prefill a 9.2K prompt in 1.08 s' conclusion is about whether one arbitrarily-chosen GPU can meet the deadline, not about the kernel's roofline regime.
findings.issue: The book repeatedly labels this comparison an 'illustrative single-device roofline argument' and warns it 'is not the evidence that prefill is compute-bound'. Yet the same warning is absent in Ch. 8 §8.3.5 and in Fig 8.2, where the prefill/decode regime split is the headline. In Ch. 8 Table 8-1's neighbour text (p. 178) the verdict row reads 'compute-bound' with the reason given as intensity, which is correct, but Ch. 2's Table 2-1 (p. 44) row 'Prefill: regime verdict — compute-bound regime' gives the derivation as 'weight-only arithmetic intensity ~9.2K FLOP/byte ... both > ridge ~295', which is consistent. The inconsistency is therefore one of disclosure, not of arithmetic: the same 1.19-vs-0.989 PFLOPS figure is used in Ch. 2, Ch. 6 and Ch. 8 without the Ch. 6 caveat attached, so a reader meeting it first in Ch. 2 can carry it as the regime proof.
findings.fix_instruction: Add the caveat at first use (Ch. 2 Table 2-1, the 'Prefill: single-H100 capacity' row) in the derivation cell: 'device-feasibility illustration; the compute-bound regime verdict follows from arithmetic intensity (≈9,200 FLOP/byte ≫ ridge ≈295), not from this rate comparison'. Repeat the pointer to Ch. 6 §6.3.3.

findings.evidence: These percentages are hypothetical telemetry signatures used to illustrate how to read utilization — not a measured benchmark find from any trace.
findings.issue: The paragraphs immediately preceding this disclaimer present 'a decode kernel pinned at ~95% of HBM bandwidth but ~30% of FLOPs' and 'a prefill kernel with ~90% FLOP utilization' as illustrative numbers, but the disclaimer appears after them and is easy to miss; the percentages appear without any tag in the running text, in a book whose stated discipline is that every load-bearing quantitative claim carries an inline Axis 1 + Axis 2 pair. The disclaimer also retroactively applies to Table 6-1's 'Resource tell' column ('high FLOP / MFU util, mid bandwidth' / 'high HBM util, low FLOP util'), which contains no numbers but inherits the same status.
findings.fix_instruction: Tag the example percentages inline: '~95% HBM / ~30% FLOPs [ILLUSTRATIVE][ASSUMPTION] — hypothetical telemetry signature', and add '[ILLUSTRATIVE]' to Table 6-1's Resource tell column header note.

findings.evidence: The dividing line is the compliant fraction f at which the throughput gain cancels: 70 × f = 48, i.e. f ≈ 68.6%, so goodput falls only when the compliant fraction drops below ~69%.
findings.issue: Recomputation: 48/70 = 0.6857 ✓ and the Scenarios' arithmetic (50 × 0.96 = 48 ✓; 70 × 0.94 = 65.8 ✓; 70 × 0.65 = 45.5 ✓) all check out. The defect is that the three scenarios' 'compliant fraction' values (96%, 94%, 65%) are labeled [ILLUSTRATIVE] but carry no measurement status and are not tied to the SLO: the chapter never states how a compliant fraction is computed from the underlying stream (e.g. fraction of tokens arriving before the p95 deadline), and 'compliant fraction falls to 65%' in Scenario C is asserted without a construction. Since the book's Ch. 14 protocol is the place where goodput is defined and measured, Scenario C's 65% — the one that carries the conclusion 'goodput falls' — needs either a construction or an explicit 'no construction given; the point is the algebra' note.
findings.fix_instruction: Add one sentence defining the compliant fraction operationally ('the fraction of emitted tokens whose arrival time is within the SLO deadline for their request'), and mark Scenario C's 65% as a constructed input: 'Scenario C: with 65% of tokens arriving after the deadline — a constructed split, not a measured stream.'

findings.chapter: Preface, Reading conventions (vs. Ch. 6 §6.3.3 source-key convention)
findings.evidence: Preface (PDF p.20, printed xiv): 'read any "meets 1.2 s" statement as conditional on a named tested workload and end-to-end timing (S-01).' Ch. 6 (PDF p.131, printed 111): 'each [S#] names one entry in the References chapter, where [S3]–[S7] resolve; Ch 11 lists [S1]–[S6] inline.' All other keys in the visible text use bracketed [S3]/[S4]/[S5]/[S6]/[S7] form.
findings.issue: The Preface's only source key is written '(S-01)' — a hyphenated, parenthesized form that does not match the book's declared '[S#]' key convention used everywhere else. A reader cannot tell whether 'S-01' is the same entry as '[S1]' or a distinct key, so the citation is not resolvable under the book's own rule ('each [S#] names one entry in the References chapter').
findings.fix_instruction: Rewrite '(S-01)' as '[S1]' (or whichever [S#] entry it denotes) so the key format matches the References-chapter convention used in Ch. 6/7/8.

findings.evidence: page 109: "Table 6-1 — Detecting the bottleneck regime" references §8.3.3 and Ch 8 roofline; recurring p.109 pointer text: "see §7" bare form
findings.issue: Bare §7 cross-reference violates Preface §N.M convention (Preface page 13: "Section cross-references use the § chapter.section form: a bare § N.M refers to chapter N, section M — so §1.4 is Ch.1, Section 4"). Bare §7 has no chapter prefix and does not resolve to existing target; should be §7.3 or §7.x. Pattern recurs p.118.
findings.fix_instruction: Replace every bare §N (e.g., §7, §24) with fully-qualified §N.M; grep document for regex "§\s*\d+\b" and resolve each against Contents existence; flag Ch24 reference that has no Chapter 24 target.

findings.evidence: page 104-105: Fig 6.1 caption "metric hierarchy as diagnostic chain" lists workload metrics box includes "concurrency"; body page 103 text: "concurrency is a serving/scheduler state (Little's law), not a workload input"
findings.issue: Figure vs body ontology contradiction: Fig 6.1 places concurrency in workload metrics vs body classifies same concurrency slot as serving/KV budget metric. Figure vs caption vs body mismatch.
findings.fix_instruction: Move concurrency entry in Fig 6.1 workload box to serving/resource layer or add footnote clarifying offered vs admitted concurrency; align caption wording with §6.1.1 classification.
